# Results — Study 766 (Memecoin-Season)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — crypto
folklore's "memecoin season": in euphoric windows the dog-coins (DOGE, SHIB) blow past Bitcoin,
and a weekly momentum rotation can harvest it net of costs, beating a BTC HODL. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (last complete calendar month; the partial current week is dropped). Fingerprint
`b75635d0b392` (BTC/DOGE/SHIB weekly close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily close for **BTC-USD, DOGE-USD, SHIB-USD** (1,902 daily rows), resampled to Friday-close weekly bars (**272** bars) |
| Common window | **2021-04-16 → 2026-06-26** — starts the day all three first carry a *positive* price. SHIB is binding: yfinance stores its sub-1e-10 launch price as literal `0.0` for ~8 months, so the tradable universe only begins April 2021 (a short, mania-dominated sample — said loudly) |
| Signal | trailing **4-week** simple return per asset, known at the week's close |
| Rotation | hold the single top-momentum coin over the **next** week (`choice.shift(1)` — one documented lag, no look-ahead); optional cash exit when all momentum ≤ 0 (not the headline variant) |
| Costs | **30 bps per leg × NAV**; a coin-to-coin switch is two legs (sell + buy). Gross **and** net reported; a 0→100 bps sweep for break-even |
| Benchmarks | BTC buy-and-hold; a weekly-rebalanced equal-weight BTC/DOGE/SHIB basket — same window for all legs |
| Price basis | price-only == total-return for crypto (no dividends) |

**Survivorship is named on the Signal axis.** DOGE and SHIB are the two memecoins that
*survived* out of thousands launched in 2020-2021. Backtesting a rotation on the two ex-post
winners is survivorship bias in its purest form — in April 2021 you did not know which two of
ten thousand indistinguishable dog-coins would still exist. Every return below is therefore an
**upper bound** a real-time trader could not have banked. A point-in-time universe including the
dead coins would push every number strictly *worse*.

## The steelman — did the memecoins actually blow past BTC? (buy-and-hold over the window)

| asset | total return |
|---|--:|
| BTC | **−5%** |
| DOGE | **−80%** |
| SHIB | **+300%** |

Only **one** of the two memecoins beat cash. The window opens in April 2021, right at DOGE's
mania peak, so DOGE lost 80% and never recovered; SHIB alone (+300%) carries the "memecoins
win" narrative. "Memecoins beat Bitcoin" is really "*the survivor that kept going up* beat
Bitcoin" — knowable only in hindsight.

## The race — momentum rotation vs BTC HODL vs equal-weight

| strategy | total return | CAGR | Sharpe | max drawdown | vol (ann.) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Momentum rotation (**gross**) | −60% | −16.4%/yr | +0.39 | −87% | — |
| Momentum rotation (**net**, 30 bps/leg) | **−73.6%** | −23.0%/yr | +0.34 | **−89%** | **162%** |
| BTC buy-and-hold | **−2.5%** | −0.5%/yr | +0.26 | −74% | 55% |
| Equal-weight basket | **+217.2%** | +25.0%/yr | +0.62 | −80% | 118% |

The rotation finishes **dead last** — below even a flat BTC hold, and a universe away from the
naive equal-weight basket. Net of 30 bps it loses 74%; it makes **68** coin-to-coin switches
(avg turnover 0.51 legs/week). The strategy meant to *harvest* one of the great speculative runs
in history lost money in it.

## Cost sweep — it isn't the fees

| cost (bps/leg) | net total | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 | **−60%** | +0.39 |
| 10 | −65% | +0.37 |
| 30 | −74% | +0.34 |
| 50 | −80% | +0.31 |
| 100 | −90% | +0.23 |

At **zero** cost the rotation still loses 60%. This is not a good strategy spoiled by fees — it
structurally buys whatever just spiked (near a local top) and sells whatever just dropped (near a
local bottom), in assets that swing ±162%/yr. **The volatility itself is the tax.**

## Is the edge over BTC real?

Paired weekly excess-over-BTC return: mean **+0.717%/week**, but **t = +0.59** (n = 267 weeks) —
nowhere near the desk's |t| ≥ 2 bar. The *positive average weekly excess with a deeply negative
compounded outcome* is the volatility tax made explicit: with 162%/yr vol, the geometric drag
(≈ −½σ² per week) is larger than the weekly edge, so a positive-mean strategy compounds to ruin.

## Random-rotation placebo — does momentum add anything?

Each week pick a coin uniformly at random (no momentum); 4,000 seeds; same costs and lag.

| | net total | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| Momentum rotation | −74% | +0.34 |
| Random rotation (median) | −72% | +0.28 |

- **p(random total ≥ momentum) = 0.517**
- **p(random Sharpe ≥ momentum) = 0.410**

A random weekly coin-pick matches or beats the momentum rotation about **half** the time. The
momentum ranking extracts no exploitable structure — a dice roll does as well.

## Where does any apparent edge live? — 2021 mania vs after

| segment | weeks | rotation (net) | BTC HODL | excess *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mania (< 2022-01) | 33 | +5.1% (Sh +1.01) | −7.2% (Sh +0.18) | +0.83 |
| after (≥ 2022-01) | 234 | **−74.8%** (Sh +0.08) | **+29.6%** (Sh +0.37) | −0.32 |

The rotation edges BTC only in the 33-week 2021 mania sliver, and even there *t* = 0.83 (not
significant); afterward it collapses 75% while BTC gains 30%. No regime shows a certified edge.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

A 3-asset synthetic weekly world with TUNABLE momentum persistence; no network.

| world | rotation-minus-equal-weight excess *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (persistence = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.06** (sd 1.15), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds |
| planted persistence = 0.35 (seed 766) | **+5.12** |

The rotation harvests momentum cleanly *when it exists* (planted t = +5.12) and sits at zero on
the null. So the real-tape verdict is not a broken backtest: memecoin weekly returns simply do
not carry the exploitable week-to-week momentum the folklore assumes. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The weekly excess-over-BTC *t* is **+0.59** (n = 267); a random-rotation
  placebo matches or beats the strategy on return **51.7%** of the time and on Sharpe **41.0%**
  of the time; no sub-period shows a certified edge. The momentum signal carries no exploitable
  information on this tape, and the raw "memecoins won" claim is one survivor (SHIB) carrying two
  losers.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of a mild 30 bps/leg the rotation returns **−73.6%** against BTC
  **−2.5%** and equal-weight **+217.2%**, with an **−89%** drawdown and **162%/yr** volatility;
  it loses **60% even at zero cost**, so the failure is structural, not fee-driven. Its one
  flattering leg — owning SHIB — is survivorship (2 winners of thousands).
- **"Beats a coin flip?" — BUSTED.** A random weekly coin pick does as well or better about half
  the time. The momentum ranking is indistinguishable from a dartboard.
